corrections.caveats: Enricher, security bug: the embedded tsf no-argument fast path checks len <= staticbuf_size + 1 and then copies len + 1 bytes, so a no-argument message of 157 or 158 characters on Linux (156 or 157 on Windows) with the date prefix writes up to 2 bytes past Log()'s 200-byte stack buffer. Harness mismatch: the README cites ~200-byte formatted messages, but test.cpp's latency bench uses ~108-114 bytes and reports the mean only; the throughput bench sends raw 200-byte LogRaw messages with no formatting; the write() bench uses 5-byte writes. Each formatted message makes a syscall(__NR_gettid) on Linux, which undercuts the README's few-syscalls argument. One mutex per Logger; producers sleep-spin when the ring is full; the writer's idle backoff grows to 1024 ms; no fsync; timestamps use the standard-time offset, one hour off during DST.

tier_reason: C stands: a competing library's README; numbers match; harness biased against Rayon.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: Fork Union's scripts/nbody.rs and propagation.rs call pool.install from the main thread, which is not a pool worker, on every round (twice per N-body iteration), taking the in_worker_cold path (global injector push plus a Mutex/Condvar LockLatch wait), while OpenMP's master thread joins the work; one install around the whole loop or use_current_thread is the idiomatic form. N-body OpenMP is pinned (OMP_PROC_BIND=spread) and the Rayon pool is not. So the Rayon numbers are pessimistic and its wins are not inflated. Minimum toolchain: published 1.12.0 declares rust_version 1.80; main's Cargo.toml says rustc 1.85, edition 2024. Gotchas: Mutex/OnceLock reentrancy deadlock (#592 open, #1251), slowdown with non-power-of-two thread counts (#968 open), quadratic stealing cost (#394 open), spawn panics abort without a panic_handler, 32 yield rounds before sleeping.
